problems.title: False generalization probability bound
assumptions: Fixed model; finite four-response space; lengths1; M2; beta=gamma=1; probability floor exp(-3)
Independent sample N1 from explicitly specified two-input population
problems.check: Exact finite-tail calculation and analytic derivative
counterevidence: Correct fixed-model concentration inequality is available
problems.impact: Invalid advertised theoretical guarantee, not empirical refutation
problems.correction: Use derivative bound1 and empirical-mean scaling; trained-parameter guarantee still needs uniformity/stability

independent_check.source_fidelity: Freshly viewed p.15 Step 2 probability bound, Step 4 derivative and Step 5 iid empirical mean; p.16 Steps 5-8 formula, ci definition and sample-sufficiency takeaway; p.5 Section 3.2.2 advertised theoretical guarantee.
independent_check.operative_assumptions: Four one-token responses, two rejected responses, beta=gamma=1, fixed singleton model class, two-input iid population with probabilities .9/.1, N=1. Both response vectors normalize and all entries satisfy the C=3 floor. No condition requires preferred responses to have larger model probability.
independent_check.independent_reasoning: Differentiating log(1+exp(-z)) gives -1/(1+exp(z)), whose magnitude exceeds 1/2 at z=-1 and -2. With z_A=-2,z_B=-1, direct enumeration of both N=1 sample outcomes yields tail .1 at epsilon=.7; the printed two-sided bound is .0396821894887. The mean replacement scale is R/N; using unaveraged ci requires N^2, not N, in the corresponding exponential form.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_alternatives: Granting rather than disputing the probability floor avoids an unrelated modeling objection. Fixing the model removes adaptive-parameter issues; hence no training-dependence interpretation rescues this finite example. Larger-sample empirical performance remains separate evidence.
independent_check.dependency_and_severity: Major: the explicit theoretical justification of Section 3.2.2 is invalid. No empirical benchmark failure or convergence failure follows from the counterexample.
independent_check.repair_scope: A fixed-model loss-range R bound 2 exp(-2N epsilon^2/R^2) is justified. Training-dependent theta still needs a uniform or stability argument. The claimed adequacy of 6000 examples is not established by this repair.

problems.title: SFT sign in Eq3 conflicts with minimization
problems.result: Written positive log term has opposite SFT direction; release uses conventional sign
problems.impact: Written objective discrepancy; no established experimental consequence

independent_check.source_fidelity: Freshly viewed source p.5 Eq.(3), lambda=.1; statically read released logo_train.py lines 271-274.
independent_check.operative_assumptions: Minimization of the displayed loss with positive lambda. The sign check concerns the regularizer component, without assuming it dominates the preference gradient.
independent_check.independent_reasoning: For a binary preferred logit t, d[lambda log sigmoid(t)]/dt=lambda(1-sigmoid(t))>0; gradient descent decreases t. Conventional positive cross-entropy has the opposite derivative. The actual released branch uses that conventional sign.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_alternatives: The release cross-entropy branch directly contradicts an implemented wrong-sign allegation; full causal-label alignment is outside this local sign check.
independent_check.dependency_and_severity: Minor written-objective inconsistency; no supported historical experimental effect.
independent_check.repair_scope: Negate the written SFT log-probability term only; this repairs its optimization direction, not the whole trainer.

problems.title: Released log-probability slicing changes two-negative objective
problems.check: Static entry-point trace and independent scalar-array diagnostic
problems.result: B1 broadcasts unintended mixed objective; B2 incompatible shapes
counterevidence: Release commit not established as historical experiment code
problems.impact: Core released implementation fidelity; historical result impact Unverifiable
problems.correction: Slice rejected2 from2*B; only local algebra verified

independent_check.source_fidelity: Static source trace from launcher to LOGOTrainer instantiation at lines 363-377, concatenation at 201-205, slices at 245-250, rejected averaging at 266 and loss mean at 269. All four source files hash-match the frozen manifest.
independent_check.operative_assumptions: Three B-row input blocks and one scalar average log probability per row; B=1 launch setting; sigmoid branch with beta=1,gamma=0 and no smoothing for the illustrative calculation only.
independent_check.independent_reasoning: At B=1 the bad second-reject slice has entries [r1,r2], so broadcast addition produces [r1,(r1+r2)/2], and the mean includes an extra one-negative loss. Direct scalar calculation yields .22009484928 versus intended .12692801104. At B=2 the summands have shapes (2,) and (4,), neither dimension equal nor one, so they are not broadcast-compatible. The separately correct logits slice begins at 2B.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_alternatives: The commit dated 2025-10-10 is a frozen retrieved release, not established as the experiment version. No author code was run, and the scalar example does not claim launcher hyperparameter reproduction.
independent_check.dependency_and_severity: Major for fidelity of the core released two-negative objective: the wrong slice changes the trained objective even at the supplied batch setting. Historical benchmark consequences remain unresolved.
independent_check.repair_scope: Starting the second-reject log-probability slice at 2B restores equal shapes and the intended local average. Full training behavior, gradients and empirical scores require further authorized work.
